verdict.rationale: Mistral's first-party prompt caching docs say requests sharing the same prefix reuse previously computed prompt tokens. Cached tokens are billed at 10% of the standard input price, and cache hits can reduce latency, so the cost, latency and pricing parts of the story are all documented. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of cache hit behavior and actual latency savings.

support.subject: As an ml-engineer, I can cut cost and latency on repeated context with documented prompt/prefix caching and its pricing

citations.quote: Prompt caching lets you reuse previously computed prompt tokens when requests share the same prefix
Cached prompt tokens are billed at 10% of the standard input token price, and cache hits can reduce response latency by reusing part of the previous prompt computation.
